key_insight: SAGEAgent turns multimodal survival prediction into an active decision problem: instead of using every available clinical modality by default, it learns when the next test is worth the cost and burden. This enables more efficient predictions by balancing accuracy with real-world acquisition constraints.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap in multimodal oncology models that either assume all modalities are always available or simply cope with missing inputs. It targets the clinical question of whether additional diagnostic modalities should be acquired at each step, given their cost, invasiveness, and limited incremental value.
method: Frames modality acquisition as a sequential, cost-aware decision process for survival prediction.
Uses a self-evolving agent to reason about which modality to acquire next based on expected predictive benefit versus acquisition burden.
Supports clinically ordered modalities, allowing the model to operate under realistic workflows where tests are obtained progressively rather than all at once.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work shifts multimodal learning from passive fusion to active information gathering under constraints. It is especially relevant for healthcare applications where reducing unnecessary tests can improve efficiency, patient comfort, and deployment realism.
visual_elements: A left-to-right pipeline showing escalating modalities from demographics to genomic profiling.
A decision-tree or agent loop illustrating when to acquire the next modality versus stop.
A trade-off chart plotting predictive gain against acquisition cost/burden.
An icon-based comparison of expensive clinical tests versus low-cost initial inputs.
paper_title: SAGEAgent: A Self-Evolving Agent for Cost-Aware Modality Acquisition in Multimodal Survival Prediction
paper_authors: Chongyu Qu, Can Cui, Zhengyi Lu, Junchao Zhu, Tianyuan Yao
